title: Provision-to-Ready: Provisioning Step Tracing Plan (spans, tags, cardinality, retention)
content:
Context / why this doc exists
We’re instrumenting the new provision-to-ready automation workflow so we can answer:
- “Where is time-to-ready spent?” (step breakdown, P50/P95, by region + GPU type)
- “What are the top failure modes and where?” (failure classes, retry behavior, quarantine)
- “Are we regressing after image changes / rollout flags?” (image channel/version correlation)

This doc is the working plan for tracing + metrics across provisioning steps. It is intentionally opinionated about tag/cardinality constraints so we don’t repeat the early rollout pain (per-node tags causing explosions).

Scope
- Orchestrator (fleet provisioning controller / automation job)
- Node validation agent (DaemonSet) and its check runner
- Fleet Readiness Service (control plane) writes + state transitions
- Optional: perf canary hook (post-provision smoke) as a nested span (not a full separate spec)

Non-goals
- Full dashboard spec (see dashboards doc / Sergio)
- Log format spec (we’ll reference log linking conventions but not mandate every field)

Principles / constraints
1) Traces are for understanding a single node’s journey; metrics are for fleet-level SLOs.
2) Metrics MUST NOT include per-node identifiers.
3) Trace attributes can include identifiers (node_id, instance_id) but ONLY on sampled traces; do not promote them into metrics via exemplars/labels.
4) Every step must emit: a span, a duration metric (histogram), and a success/failure counter.
5) Failure reasons are modeled as low-cardinality enums (“failure_class”, “failure_code”) + freeform text goes to logs/artifacts only.

Trace model (high-level)
We model a single “node bring-up” as one trace with a shared trace_id across components.
- Root span created by orchestrator at start of provisioning for a specific node.
- Child spans for each step (allocate, image, join cluster, validations, readiness write).
- Validation agent spans should be linked/parented to the orchestrator trace where feasible.
- Fleet Readiness Service spans should be linked to the same trace_id on API calls.

Propagation plan
- Orchestrator -> Fleet Readiness Service: HTTP/gRPC with W3C trace context (traceparent/tracestate). Standard OTel instrumentation.
- Orchestrator -> Validation Agent:
  - Preferred: orchestrator triggers validation via a request carrying trace context (e.g., k8s Job annotation + env var TRACEPARENT, or HTTP call to agent endpoint).
  - If we can’t get strict parent/child semantics, use Span Links:
    - Agent creates a local root span “node.validation.run” and adds a link to the orchestrator span context.
- Validation artifacts (log bundle pointers) should store trace_id in the artifact metadata so runbooks can jump from readiness failure -> trace.

Span naming conventions
- Format: <domain>.<subsystem>.<action>
- Use dots (.) not slashes; keep names stable (dashboards/alerts depend on them).
- Steps should be enumerated and shared between orchestrator and readiness service.

Canonical span list (minimum viable)
Root span
- Span: fleet.provisioning.node_bringup
  - Starts: when node is “Allocated” (as defined in ADR-017)
  - Ends: when node becomes Ready or Quarantined (terminal), OR when workflow times out

Orchestrator child spans (examples; exact steps depend on cloud/provider)
- fleet.provisioning.allocate_instance
- fleet.provisioning.configure_os (cloud-init, baseline config)
- fleet.provisioning.install_gpu_stack (driver/CUDA/NCCL as applicable; may be image bake step rather than runtime)
- fleet.provisioning.k8s_join
- fleet.provisioning.wait_node_ready (kubelet ready + CNI ready)
- fleet.provisioning.start_validation_agent (daemonset presence / agent heartbeat)
- fleet.provisioning.request_validations
- fleet.provisioning.publish_readiness_state (write to readiness service)

Validation agent spans
- fleet.validation.run (parented or linked)
  - fleet.validation.gpu_health
  - fleet.validation.driver_parity
  - fleet.validation.network_smoke
  - fleet.validation.storage_smoke
  - fleet.validation.nccl_smoke
  - fleet.validation.runtime_smoke (lightweight inference / container pull / GPU access)

Readiness service spans
- fleet.readiness.write_state
- fleet.readiness.write_artifact
- fleet.readiness.fetch_state (read path for internal UI; optional)

Perf canary (if enabled)
- fleet.canary.post_provision
  - include model name as a tag ONLY if it’s from an allowlist (low cardinality)

Span status + error handling
- Span status:
  - OK: step succeeded
  - ERROR: step failed and is either terminal OR triggers retry
- For retries:
  - Emit one span per attempt (recommended) with attribute retry_attempt=N
  - Parent “request_validations” span may wrap multiple attempts
- Do not attach raw error messages as attributes. Put them in logs, reference via artifact pointers.

Required attributes (trace)
These should be present on root span and inherited/duplicated on key step spans.
Low-cardinality attributes (safe for metrics labels if needed)
- region: e.g., us-east-1
- cloud: aws|gcp|azure (enum)
- gpu_type: a100|h100|l40s|… (enum)
- pool_type: dedicated|shared (enum)
- image_channel: candidate|stable (enum)
- rollout_flag: on|off (enum) OR rollout_stage: stage0|stage1|… (small enum)
- step_name: from canonical list (enum) (for step-level metrics)
- result: success|failure|timeout|canceled (enum)
- failure_class: gpu|driver|k8s|network|storage|nccl|runtime|control_plane|unknown (enum)
- failure_code: short enum list maintained in code (see below)

Medium-cardinality attributes (allowed in traces; avoid in metrics)
- image_version: e.g., 2025-10-07.1 (bounded but can grow; do not label all metrics by it)
- instance_type: p4d.24xlarge / etc (bounded-ish; acceptable in traces)
- kube_cluster: internal cluster name (bounded-ish; acceptable in traces)

High-cardinality attributes (trace-only; MUST NOT appear as metric labels)
- node_id (internal UUID)
- instance_id
- hostname
- ipv4/ipv6
- request_id (per API call)

Failure_code guidance
- Use short, stable enums that can be searched and graphed.
- Examples:
  - GPU_HEALTH_ECC_HIGH
  - GPU_HEALTH_XID_SEEN
  - DRIVER_MISMATCH
  - K8S_JOIN_TIMEOUT
  - CNI_NOT_READY
  - NCCL_ALLREDUCE_TIMEOUT
  - STORAGE_IOPS_BELOW_THRESHOLD
  - READINESS_WRITE_CONFLICT
- Store raw stderr / vendor-specific codes in artifact logs (S3 pointer, etc.).

Metrics plan
Metric namespace/prefix (proposed)
- fleet.provisioning.* for orchestrator step metrics
- fleet.validation.* for validation agent metrics
- fleet.readiness.* for readiness service API metrics

Core SLIs (these should exist even if tracing isn’t enabled)
- fleet.provisioning.time_to_ready_seconds (histogram)
  - Labels: region, gpu_type, pool_type, image_channel
- fleet.provisioning.success_total (counter)
  - Labels: region, gpu_type, pool_type, image_channel
- fleet.provisioning.failure_total (counter)
  - Labels: region, gpu_type, pool_type, image_channel, failure_class, failure_code
- fleet.provisioning.quarantine_total (counter)
  - Labels: region, gpu_type, pool_type, image_channel, failure_class, failure_code

Step breakdown metrics
- fleet.provisioning.step_duration_seconds (histogram)
  - Labels: region, gpu_type, pool_type, image_channel, step_name
- fleet.provisioning.step_attempts_total (counter)
  - Labels: region, gpu_type, pool_type, image_channel, step_name, result

Validation-specific metrics
- fleet.validation.check_duration_seconds (histogram)
  - Labels: region, gpu_type, pool_type, image_channel, check_name
- fleet.validation.check_failure_total (counter)
  - Labels: region, gpu_type, pool_type, image_channel, check_name, failure_code

Readiness service metrics
- fleet.readiness.write_latency_seconds (histogram)
  - Labels: region, route (enum), result
- fleet.readiness.conflict_total (counter)
  - Labels: region, route

Cardinality constraints (hard rules)
- Allowed metric labels MUST be from a controlled enum list.
- Do not label by:
  - node_id / instance_id / hostname
  - pool_id (unless we confirm it’s bounded for a given deployment; assume NOT safe)
  - image_version (unless used only in logs or as trace attribute)
  - error_message
- region x gpu_type x pool_type x image_channel x step_name is already “heavy”; keep other labels minimal.
- For internal debugging of a specific pool: use trace search (attributes) + readiness artifacts, not metric labels.

Trace sampling + retention
Tracing retention proposal (subject to platform defaults)
- Default retention: 14 days
- Sampling:
  - Head-based: 1% of successful bring-ups
  - Tail-based (or rules-based) always-sample for:
    - Any trace with result=failure
    - Any trace with quarantine action
    - Any trace with time_to_ready_seconds > P95 threshold (dynamic) or > 45m (static backstop)
- During staged rollout: temporarily increase successful sampling to 5% for the enabled region/GPU type only.

Metrics retention
- Standard metrics retention: 13 months (for seasonality + capacity planning)
- Histograms: keep default bucket cardinality; avoid per-route/per-check explosions.

Log + artifact retention (notes)
- Validation artifacts (bundles) retention: 30 days (enough for incident reviews + support escalations)
- Logs should include: trace_id, node_id, step_name, failure_code, readiness_state.
- If artifact storage costs spike, we can shorten successful artifact retention (e.g., 7 days) while keeping failed/quarantine artifacts at 30 days.

Implementation notes / where instrumentation lives
- Orchestrator: OpenTelemetry SDK (service name fleet-orchestrator) + span creation around each step function.
- Validation agent: OpenTelemetry SDK (service name node-validation-agent) with explicit spans per check.
- Readiness service: standard server instrumentation; add manual spans for state machine transitions where needed.
- Ensure consistent “step_name” and “check_name” enums are shared via a small library/package (or generated constants) to avoid drift.

Dashboards / how we’ll use this
- Step breakdown view: rely on fleet.provisioning.step_duration_seconds with step_name.
- Failure heatmap: failure_total by failure_class/failure_code.
- Trace exemplars: allowed only on histograms that do not carry high-cardinality labels; exemplars may include trace_id but not node_id.

Open questions / decisions needed
1) Do we want pool_id in metrics? Current recommendation: NO. If needed, add it only in traces and readiness artifacts.
2) Where to store trace_id so runbooks can jump from readiness UI -> trace? Proposal: readiness service stores trace_id on the node readiness record (field: last_trace_id).
3) Tail-sampling support: do we already have collector-level tail sampling in Dedicated clusters, or is this hosted-only? If not, we’ll implement rules-based “always trace on error” at the SDK level.
4) Enum governance: who approves new failure_code values? Proposal: Infra owns (Vanessa/Gabe), Observability reviews for cardinality.

Next steps
- [Sergio] Confirm metric names/buckets align with observability-pack conventions.
- [Gabe] Wire trace context from orchestrator -> validation agent (at least via span links).
- [Benji/Jordan] Add trace_id storage to readiness records + expose in readiness API response.
- [Aisha] Validate sampling/retention won’t break SLO alerting; alerts remain metric-based.

Appendix: quick reference (do/don’t)
DO
- Use step_name/check_name enums
- Use failure_class + failure_code
- Store raw error text in logs/artifacts
- Use traces to debug a single node’s failures

DON’T
- Put node_id/instance_id/pool_id into metric labels
- Put raw error messages into span attributes
- Add new labels without checking cardinality impact
